reference.title: Development of bifunctional biosensors for sensing and dynamic control of glycolysis flux in metabolic engineering

target.condition: Dose-response with extracellular FBP 0.001-400 mM + 10 g/L acetate (pL18, Fig. 2D); other culture conditions unknown (Methods absent).

trigger.observation: Few biosensors exist for central glycolytic metabolites; glycolysis flux imbalance (overflow at high flux, poor growth at low flux) lacks autonomous regulation systems.
trigger.reasoning: Create and tune positive-response FBP biosensors (pL01-pL10; refined pL15-pL18) with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges.

evidence.description: Fluorescence output; intracellular FBP concentration; Hill-fit dynamic range and EC50.
evidence.source_location: CK- (no pL18 plasmid), CK (0 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP), 0 (10 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Dose-response curves measured in vivo and Hill-fitted (Fig. 2A,C,E).
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Promoter-architecture engineering of Cra-regulated promoters (core promoter strength, TFBS position, Cra-box sequence) to build pL01-pL10 and refined pL15-pL18.

result.metric: Fluorescence output; intracellular FBP concentration; Hill-fit dynamic range and EC50.
result.after: Series of positive-response biosensors with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges obtained; pL18 used later for glmS activation module.

decision_chain.rule: When building an FBP/Cra-based glycolysis-flux sensor in E. coli, tune core promoter strength, TFBS position and Cra-box affinity so the sensor threshold and dynamic range span the physiological intracellular FBP range, because sensor output is set by the FBP-Cra-DNA equilibrium. (Validated only for Cra/FBP biosensors in E. coli in this paper.)

target.condition: Dose-response with extracellular FBP 0.001-400 mM + 10 g/L acetate (pL18, Fig. 2D); other culture conditions unknown (Methods absent).

trigger.observation: Initial promoter variants did not cover desired thresholds/dynamic ranges (implied by need for further tuning axes).
trigger.reasoning: Create and tune positive-response FBP biosensors (pL01-pL10; refined pL15-pL18) with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges.

evidence.description: Fluorescence output; intracellular FBP concentration; Hill-fit dynamic range and EC50.
evidence.source_location: CK- (no pL18 plasmid), CK (0 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP), 0 (10 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Resulting sensors characterized by measured dose-response (Fig. 2C,E).

alternatives.approach: Cra-overexpressing plasmid sensors were later excluded from application cases because of Cra's global regulatory impact (4_discussion_p004).

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Tuning by Cra overexpression and by mutating Cra ligand-binding affinity (positive-response branch, Fig. 2B).

result.metric: Fluorescence output; intracellular FBP concentration; Hill-fit dynamic range and EC50.
result.after: Series of positive-response biosensors with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges obtained; pL18 used later for glmS activation module.

decision_chain.rule: When a TF-based metabolite sensor's threshold is mismatched to the in vivo effector range in E. coli, adjust regulator expression level or ligand-binding affinity of the TF, because both shift the occupancy equilibrium of the operator. (Validated for Cra/FBP in E. coli only.)

target.condition: Dose-response characterization; culture conditions unknown (Methods absent).

trigger.observation: Need to down-regulate glycolysis (pfkA) autonomously when FBP (flux proxy) is high; positive-response sensors alone cannot repress.
trigger.reasoning: Create and tune negative-response FBP biosensors (pL19-pL30; pL35 with Cra aa57-60 mutations).

evidence.source_location: Not stated for this characterization beyond biosensor series comparison.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured dose-response curves and Hill fits (Fig. 3A,C); pL35 characterized by dose-response (Fig. 3B).
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Promoter engineering to convert Cra regulation into negative-response output (pL19-pL30); site mutagenesis of Cra at amino acids 57-60 under P23102 (pL35).

result.after: Negative-response biosensors pL19-pL30 and pL35 obtained; pL19 (Ppam) and pL25 (Ppar) selected for genome integration at pfkA.

decision_chain.rule: When a pathway gene must be repressed at high glycolysis flux in E. coli, place Cra TFBS so that FBP-bound Cra relieves/reorganizes repression to yield negative FBP-response, and tune via Cra ligand-affinity mutations, because regulation sign and dose-response are set by TFBS position and TF-ligand affinity. (Validated for Cra-based circuits in E. coli only.)

target.condition: Shake flask; 1-L fermenter 120 h; feeding/medium unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Figs. 6-7 not available).

trigger.observation: Prior EP-bifido design (Wang et al. 2019) requires sufficient F6P and NADPH supply from the PP pathway; natural glycolysis was previously blocked by permanent pfkA deletion.
trigger.reasoning: Replace static pfkA knockout in the EP-bifido pathway with FBP-responsive dynamic repression to resolve growth/production trade-off and maximize MVA.

evidence.description: MVA titer and carbon yield; growth; glucose uptake; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP.
evidence.source_location: Non-regulated BW-Pzwf::P23109; prior static-knockout BW-delta-pfkA EP-bifido (background_citation benchmark, Wang et al. 2019); IPTG-CRISPRi strain (background_citation benchmark, Li et al. 2021).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Resulting strain phenotypes (growth, glucose uptake, MVA) measured in this study.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Genomic replacement of the zwf promoter with the stronger P23109 promoter (strain BW-Pzwf::P23109).

result.metric: MVA titer and carbon yield; growth; glucose uptake; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP.
result.after: BW-PR: 73.31 g/L MVA, 63.00 mol% carbon yield, <0.1 g/L acetate, stationary phase after 12 h, FBP drop after 15 h; fermenter: 111.3 g/L at 120 h, no by-products. BW-PMT accumulated <2.47 g/L acetate.

decision_chain.rule: When an EP-bifido-type acetyl-CoA/F6P supply pathway in E. coli is limited by PP pathway throughput, up-regulate zwf via a stronger constitutive promoter, because Zwf controls carbon entry into the PP pathway that delivers F6P and NADPH. (Validated for MVA production in this E. coli EP-bifido system.)

target.condition: Shake flask; 1-L fermenter 120 h; feeding/medium unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Figs. 6-7 not available).

trigger.observation: Permanent pfkA deletion severely suppressed growth and glucose uptake, capping MVA at 11.02 g/L despite 64.3 mol% yield - a measured growth/production trade-off demanding dynamic instead of static control.
trigger.reasoning: Replace static pfkA knockout in the EP-bifido pathway with FBP-responsive dynamic repression to resolve growth/production trade-off and maximize MVA.

evidence.description: MVA titer and carbon yield; growth; glucose uptake; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP.
evidence.source_location: Non-regulated BW-Pzwf::P23109; prior static-knockout BW-delta-pfkA EP-bifido (background_citation benchmark, Wang et al. 2019); IPTG-CRISPRi strain (background_citation benchmark, Li et al. 2021).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured titers, growth, mRNA and FBP time courses for BW-PMT/BW-PR vs non-regulated control.

alternatives.approach: IPTG-induced CRISPRi repression of pfkA (Li et al. 2021) - external-inducer strategy; yielded only 8.53 g/L MVA (0.12x of BW-PR) and requires inducer timing; cited as inferior benchmark (background_citation).

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Genomic replacement of the pfkA promoter with negative-response biosensor promoters Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding BW-PMT and BW-PR (dynamic EP-bifido pathway).

result.metric: MVA titer and carbon yield; growth; glucose uptake; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP.
result.after: BW-PR: 73.31 g/L MVA, 63.00 mol% carbon yield, <0.1 g/L acetate, stationary phase after 12 h, FBP drop after 15 h; fermenter: 111.3 g/L at 120 h, no by-products. BW-PMT accumulated <2.47 g/L acetate.

decision_chain.rule: When static knockout of an essential glycolytic step (e.g., pfkA) in E. coli collapses growth and substrate uptake, replace the native promoter with a biosensor promoter negatively responsive to intracellular FBP, because FBP reports glycolytic flux and enables automatic growth-then-production switching. (Validated for MVA via EP-bifido in E. coli; extended to GlcNAc in EXP5.)

target.condition: Glucose as sole carbon source; shake-flask production implied; detailed conditions unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Fig. 8 unavailable).

trigger.observation: Lower glycolysis is a competitive pathway for GlcNAc synthesis from glucose; F6P is the shared precursor, so pfkA must be down-regulated.
trigger.reasoning: Balance glycolysis and GlcNAc biosynthesis at the F6P node by dynamically repressing pfkA and/or activating glmS.
trigger.source_location: E. coli DN5 (DH5alpha derivative, delta-nag delta-ackA delta-poxB delta-ldhA delta-nan; constructed in previous studies - background)

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Genomic replacement of pfkA promoter in DN5 with Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding DN5-IM and DN5-PM.

result.metric: GlcNAc titer; growth; glucose consumption; intracellular FBP.
result.after: DN5-IM 8.65 g/L; DN5-GM 6.33; DN5-GAR 7.98; DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L; dual regulation not obviously higher than single; FBP lower in DN5-IM/DN5-IMM, unchanged in DN5-GAR. DN5-IMAR titer not reported in available text.

decision_chain.rule: When a product draws fructose-6-phosphate as precursor in glucose-grown E. coli, dynamically repress pfkA with an FBP-negative-response promoter, because this diverts F6P from lower glycolysis to the product while preserving early growth. (Validated for GlcNAc in the DN5 background.)

target.condition: Glucose as sole carbon source; shake-flask production implied; detailed conditions unknown (Methods absent; Supplementary Fig. 8 unavailable).

trigger.observation: glmS needs up-regulation for GlcNAc overproduction, but early-stage overexpression may cause bacterial lysis and growth inhibition (Deng et al. 2005), so constitutive strong expression is unsuitable.
trigger.reasoning: Balance glycolysis and GlcNAc biosynthesis at the F6P node by dynamically repressing pfkA and/or activating glmS.
trigger.source_location: E. coli DN5 (DH5alpha derivative, delta-nag delta-ackA delta-poxB delta-ldhA delta-nan; constructed in previous studies - background)

evidence.description: GlcNAc titer; growth; glucose consumption; intracellular FBP.

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Plasmid-based dynamic activation of glmS using positive-response promoters PM23107 (pBacm) and PR23107-cra plus cra/P23102 (pBacar), transformed into DN5 to give DN5-GM and DN5-GAR.

result.metric: GlcNAc titer; growth; glucose consumption; intracellular FBP.
result.after: DN5-IM 8.65 g/L; DN5-GM 6.33; DN5-GAR 7.98; DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L; dual regulation not obviously higher than single; FBP lower in DN5-IM/DN5-IMM, unchanged in DN5-GAR. DN5-IMAR titer not reported in available text.

decision_chain.rule: When overexpression of a product-pathway enzyme is toxic in early growth (e.g., glmS in E. coli), drive it with a positive-response biosensor promoter activated as FBP accumulates, because induction is delayed until the production phase, avoiding lysis. (Validated for GlcNAc in DN5.)

decision_chain.rule: When single dynamic repression of pfkA already restores most of the achievable F6P-to-GlcNAc flux in E. coli DN5, adding dynamic glmS activation on top gives no obvious further titer gain, because the node flux is already saturated by competitor repression. (Observed only in this DN5/GlcNAc context; do not generalize.)

nodes.trigger: Need to down-regulate glycolysis (pfkA) autonomously when FBP (flux proxy) is high; positive-response sensors alone cannot repress.

nodes.decision_summary: Genomic replacement of the zwf promoter with the stronger P23109 promoter (strain BW-Pzwf::P23109).
nodes.trigger: Prior EP-bifido design (Wang et al. 2019) requires sufficient F6P and NADPH supply from the PP pathway; natural glycolysis was previously blocked by permanent pfkA deletion.

nodes.decision_summary: Genomic replacement of the pfkA promoter with negative-response biosensor promoters Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding BW-PMT and BW-PR (dynamic EP-bifido pathway).
nodes.trigger: Permanent pfkA deletion severely suppressed growth and glucose uptake, capping MVA at 11.02 g/L despite 64.3 mol% yield - a measured growth/production trade-off demanding dynamic instead of static control.

nodes.decision_summary: Genomic replacement of pfkA promoter in DN5 with Ppam (pL19) or Ppar (pL25), yielding DN5-IM and DN5-PM.
nodes.trigger: Lower glycolysis is a competitive pathway for GlcNAc synthesis from glucose; F6P is the shared precursor, so pfkA must be down-regulated.

nodes.decision_summary: Plasmid-based dynamic activation of glmS using positive-response promoters PM23107 (pBacm) and PR23107-cra plus cra/P23102 (pBacar), transformed into DN5 to give DN5-GM and DN5-GAR.
nodes.trigger: glmS needs up-regulation for GlcNAc overproduction, but early-stage overexpression may cause bacterial lysis and growth inhibition (Deng et al. 2005), so constitutive strong expression is unsuitable.

nodes.decision_summary: Simultaneous dynamic repression of pfkA and activation of glmS (pBacm or pBacar into DN5-IM), yielding DN5-IMM and DN5-IMAR.
nodes.trigger: Hypothesis that combining both arms of node control (repress competitor + activate product path) would further raise GlcNAc titer.

nodes.decision_summary: Verify that biosensor output tracks intracellular FBP and glycolysis flux across strains with graded glycolytic defects.
nodes.trigger: Negative-response biosensors pL19-pL30 and pL35 obtained; pL19 (Ppam) and pL25 (Ppar) selected for genome integration at pfkA.

engineering_logic_chain.goal: Design, construct and tune bifunctional (positive- and negative-response) glycolysis-flux biosensors based on the Cra-FBP pair that sense intracellular fructose-1,6-diphosphate (FBP) and dynamically regulate glycolysis flux, then apply them to balance biosynthesis of mevalonate (MVA) and N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) in Escherichia coli.
engineering_logic_chain.initial_bottleneck: Few biosensors exist for central glycolytic metabolites; glycolysis flux imbalance (overflow at high flux, poor growth at low flux) lacks autonomous regulation systems.
engineering_logic_chain.hypothesis: Create and tune positive-response FBP biosensors (pL01-pL10; refined pL15-pL18) with varied thresholds/dynamic ranges.

rule_provenance.rule: When building an FBP/Cra-based glycolysis-flux sensor in E. coli, tune core promoter strength, TFBS position and Cra-box affinity so the sensor threshold and dynamic range span the physiological intracellular FBP range, because sensor output is set by the FBP-Cra-DNA equilibrium. (Validated only for Cra/FBP biosensors in E. coli in this paper.)

When a TF-based metabolite sensor's threshold is mismatched to the in vivo effector range in E. coli, adjust regulator expression level or ligand-binding affinity of the TF, because both shift the occupancy equilibrium of the operator. (Validated for Cra/FBP in E. coli only.)

When a pathway gene must be repressed at high glycolysis flux in E. coli, place Cra TFBS so that FBP-bound Cra relieves/reorganizes repression to yield negative FBP-response, and tune via Cra ligand-affinity mutations, because regulation sign and dose-response are set by TFBS position and TF-ligand affinity. (Validated for Cra-based circuits in E. coli only.)

When an EP-bifido-type acetyl-CoA/F6P supply pathway in E. coli is limited by PP pathway throughput, up-regulate zwf via a stronger constitutive promoter, because Zwf controls carbon entry into the PP pathway that delivers F6P and NADPH. (Validated for MVA production in this E. coli EP-bifido system.)

When static knockout of an essential glycolytic step (e.g., pfkA) in E. coli collapses growth and substrate uptake, replace the native promoter with a biosensor promoter negatively responsive to intracellular FBP, because FBP reports glycolytic flux and enables automatic growth-then-production switching. (Validated for MVA via EP-bifido in E. coli; extended to GlcNAc in EXP5.)

When a product draws fructose-6-phosphate as precursor in glucose-grown E. coli, dynamically repress pfkA with an FBP-negative-response promoter, because this diverts F6P from lower glycolysis to the product while preserving early growth. (Validated for GlcNAc in the DN5 background.)

When overexpression of a product-pathway enzyme is toxic in early growth (e.g., glmS in E. coli), drive it with a positive-response biosensor promoter activated as FBP accumulates, because induction is delayed until the production phase, avoiding lysis. (Validated for GlcNAc in DN5.)

When single dynamic repression of pfkA already restores most of the achievable F6P-to-GlcNAc flux in E. coli DN5, adding dynamic glmS activation on top gives no obvious further titer gain, because the node flux is already saturated by competitor repression. (Observed only in this DN5/GlcNAc context; do not generalize.)
